hints: Differentiate the curve equation implicitly with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a function of $x$.
Use the chain rule on $y^3$ and the product rule on $2xy$: their derivatives are $3y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and $2y+2x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.
Set the derivative of the left side equal to zero, gather all terms containing $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, and divide to isolate it.
walkthrough:
Differentiate each term of the implicit equation $x^3 + y^3 + 2xy + 8 = 0$ with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^3) + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(y^3) + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(2xy) + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(8) = 0$$

Compute the derivatives of each term:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^3) = 3x^2$$
Using the chain rule, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(y^3) = 3y^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$
Using the product rule, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(2xy) = 2y + 2x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(8) = 0$$

Combine all differentiated terms into one equation:
$$3x^2 + 3y^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + 2y + 2x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$$

Group the terms containing $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on the left-hand side and move other terms to the right-hand side:
$$(3y^2 + 2x)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -(3x^2 + 2y)$$

ai_rubric.Implicit Differentiation: Identifies $3y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ as the derivative of $y^3$; Identifies $2y+2x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ as the derivative of $2xy$; Concludes with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{3x^2+2y}{3y^2+2x}$.

hints: Find the two points first: setting $x=0$ or $y=0$ in the curve gives $(0,-2)$ and $(-2,0)$.
Substitute each point into the derivative from part (a) to obtain the two tangent gradients.
If the tangent angles are $A$ and $B$, use $\tan(A-B)=\dfrac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1m_2}$.
Choose the positive value corresponding to the acute angle $\alpha$ and simplify it exactly.
walkthrough:
Find the coordinates of the points where the curve crosses the coordinate axes:
When $x = 0$:
$$0^3 + y^3 + 2(0)y + 8 = 0 \implies y^3 + 8 = 0 \implies y^3 = -8 \implies y = -2$$
So the curve crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, -2)$.
When $y = 0$:
$$x^3 + 0^3 + 2x(0) + 8 = 0 \implies x^3 + 8 = 0 \implies x^3 = -8 \implies x = -2$$
So the curve crosses the $x$-axis at $(-2, 0)$.

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $(0, -2)$ using the formula from part (a):
$$m_1 = \left. \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \right|_{(0, -2)} = -\dfrac{3(0)^2 + 2(-2)}{3(-2)^2 + 2(0)} = -\dfrac{-4}{3(4)} = -\dfrac{-4}{12} = \dfrac{4}{12} = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $(-2, 0)$:
$$m_2 = \left. \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \right|_{(-2, 0)} = -\dfrac{3(-2)^2 + 2(0)}{3(0)^2 + 2(-2)} = -\dfrac{3(4)}{-4} = -\dfrac{12}{-4} = 3$$

Use the compound angle formula for the tangent of the angle between two straight lines with gradients $m_1$ and $m_2$:
$$\tan\alpha = \left| \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$$

Substitute $m_1 = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $m_2 = 3$ into the formula:
$$m_2 - m_1 = 3 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{9}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}$$
$$1 + m_1 m_2 = 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)(3) = 1 + 1 = 2$$
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{8/3}{2} = \dfrac{8}{3 \times 2} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Gradients: Finds the gradient at either $(0,-2)$ or $(-2,0)$; Derives the two gradients $\dfrac13$ and $3$; Concludes with $\tan\alpha=\dfrac43$.
